## Goal

Read a SPICE-flavored `.net` deck and resolve it into a node map plus the device records
`va-cli` turns into `ModelInstance`s — the entry point into the whole simulator for anyone who
doesn't want to write Rust to describe a circuit.

## Where it fits

```
 circuits/*.net ──[va-netlist::parser::parse]──► Netlist{nodes, devices, analysis, tran, dc}
```

`va-netlist` depends only on `va-abi` (just enough to name the ground sentinel,
`va_abi::reference::GROUND`) — it has no idea what a `ModelInstance` implementation looks like;
that dispatch happens one layer up, in `va-cli` (`t6-integration/02-cli.qmd`).

## The idea

**One line, one element or dot-card**, whitespace-tokenized, `*` full-line comments. Net `0`/
`gnd` is the reference node and never gets an unknown index; every other net gets a dense index
in first-seen order.

**Every model-referencing multi-terminal element follows the same pattern, added one letter at a
time as each ladder rung needed it**: `D<name> p n model` (two-terminal, ladder rung 2's diode),
`M<name> d g s model` (three-terminal, SPICE's own drain/gate/source order, ladder rung 5's
MOSFET — no separate body/bulk terminal, a stated v1 simplification), `Q<name> c b e model`
(three-terminal, SPICE's own collector/base/emitter order, ladder rung 6's BJT — no substrate
terminal, mirroring `M`'s own simplification). None of these needed a new *concept* in the
parser — `Device::terminals` was already `Vec<usize>`, arbitrary length, from the start.

**A `.dc <source> <start> <stop> <step>` sweep only steps a voltage source**, matching the LRM/
SPICE convention — `va-cli` reports a clear error if `source` doesn't resolve to one, rather than
silently sweeping something else.

**A `V` source distinguishes its DC value from its full time-domain waveform.** `DC <value>` or a
bare number sets `Device::value` directly; `SIN(offset amplitude freq)` sets `Device::value` to
the offset (what a DC operating point needs) *and* records the full `Waveform::Sin` separately —
because `va_abi::ModelInstance::load` deliberately has no time parameter (Interface β's own
"no time on the bridge" design, `shared/01-interfaces.qmd`), so a transient consumer needs the
full waveform to reconstruct a fresh, differently-valued source instance every step.

## The code

```rust
pub struct Netlist {
    pub nodes: HashMap<String, usize>,
    pub node_order: Vec<String>,       // first-seen order, for reporting
    pub devices: Vec<Device>,
    pub analysis: AnalysisCard,        // .op / .dc / .tran / .ac
    pub tran: Option<(f64, f64)>,      // .tran <tstep> <tstop>
    pub dc: Option<DcSweep>,           // .dc <source> <start> <stop> <step>
}

pub struct Device {
    pub name: String,
    pub model: String,                 // "resistor"/"capacitor"/"vsource", or a named model
    pub terminals: Vec<usize>,         // arbitrary length — 2 for R/C/D, 3 for M/Q
    pub value: Option<f64>,
    pub waveform: Option<Waveform>,    // Some only for a SIN-driven V source
}
```

SI scale suffixes (`3.3Meg`, `10n`, `1k`) resolve at parse time via the same scale-letter table
the lexer uses (`t1-frontend/01-lexing.qmd`) — `T G M K k m u n p f a`, `M`/`m` case-sensitive.

## It works

```console
$ cargo test -p va-netlist
running 10 tests
test tests::parses_mos_dc_devices ... ok
test tests::parses_ring_osc_devices ... ok
test tests::parses_diode_iv_sweep_card ... ok
test tests::parses_rectifier_devices_and_card ... ok
test parser::tests::value_suffixes ... ok
test parser::tests::source_values ... ok
...
test result: ok. 10 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out; finished in 0.00s
```

Every test parses a real, committed circuit file — `circuits/mos_dc.net`, `circuits/ring_osc.net`,
etc. — not a synthetic fixture invented for the test alone, so a parser regression on a real deck
would be caught here before it ever reached `va-cli`.

## Limitations

Stated in the parser module's own doc comment: subcircuits (`X`), mutual inductance (`K`),
and `.model` cards are not parsed — a device's *model* is
always resolved by `va-cli` matching a name against either a compiled `.va` file or a
hand-written `va-abi` reference primitive, never by an in-deck SPICE `.model` card.
(Inductors and all four controlled sources were on this list until 2026-08-31; they are
parsed now. `F`/`H` were the last to land because their controlling quantity is another
element's branch current, so that element has to be resolved to a row before the source can be
built — and it may be written later in the deck, which is why instances are built in two
phases.) A `.dc` sweep only steps one source linearly; no nested/
multi-source sweeps, no bare `.dc` (source-list) form some SPICE dialects accept. A `V` source's
optional trailing `SIN` parameters (delay, damping, phase) aren't parsed.

`E` and `G` are the linear voltage-controlled sources (added 2026-08-31), each taking four
nodes — the driven pair, then the controlling pair — and a gain or transconductance:
`E1 out gnd ctl gnd 4` holds `V(out) = 4*V(ctl)`, while `G1 out gnd ctl gnd 2e-3` pushes
`2e-3*V(ctl)` amps through whatever `out` is connected to. The `G` claims no branch unknown at
all; the `E` claims one, exactly as an independent source does, because it states a constraint
rather than contributing a current.

`F` and `H` are their current-controlled counterparts: two nodes, then the *name* of an
element whose branch current controls them, then a gain (`F`) or a transresistance in ohms
(`H`). That element must own a branch row — a `V` source, an `L`, an `E` or an `H` — which is
the same restriction SPICE has, and the reason its decks conventionally insert a 0 V source
purely to sense a current. Naming something without one (a resistor) is an error that says so.

A model-referencing device (`D`/`M`/`Q`) may set the model's parameters by name,
`D1 in gnd diode Is=1e-12 N=1.3` (added 2026-08-31). Before that a device could override only
the model's *first* parameter, positionally, through the SPICE scalar value — which for a
Verilog-A simulator is both limiting (models declare many parameters) and fragile, since
reordering `parameter` declarations in a `.va` file would change what every existing deck
means. An override naming a parameter the model does not declare is an error listing the ones
it does, rather than a silent no-op: a dropped override leaves a deck looking like it set
something it did not, which is precisely what the feature exists to prevent.

`PULSE(v1 v2 td tr tf pw per)` (added 2026-08-31) is the other supported waveform. Its optional
trailing parameters default the way SPICE defaults them — an omitted rise/fall is one timestep,
an omitted width or period runs to the end of the analysis — which means they depend on the
`.tran` card, and that card may appear *after* the source line. So they are filled in by a
post-pass once the whole deck has been read (`resolve_pulse_defaults`), not defaulted inline
against timing that has not been parsed yet.

`L` (inductor, added 2026-08-31) parses like `R`/`C` but behaves like a voltage source
structurally: it claims its own branch-current unknown, because its row is the constitutive law
`-(V(p)-V(n)) + d(L*i)/dt = 0` rather than a KCL sum. Writing it that way puts the flux `L*i` on
the existing charge channel, so **no Interface beta change was needed** — and the same
formulation gives the correct DC answer for free, since with no charge channel in a DC solve the
row collapses to `V(p) = V(n)`, an inductor's short circuit. Mutual inductance (`K`) is not
parsed. `IC=` on an `L` is **amps through it** (an inductor's state), seeded onto its branch
row rather than across its terminals — the units differ from a capacitor's `IC=` because the
state does.

A reactive element's `IC=` (added 2026-08-31) seeds a **transient** run only, as SPICE's `UIC`
semantics do — no DC operating point is solved first, and a `.op`/`.dc`/`.ac` run ignores it.
Conditions are applied in device order, each reading whatever its negative terminal holds at that
point, so a grounded capacitor (the case SPICE decks overwhelmingly write, and the only kind in
this zoo) is exact, while a genuinely floating one that nothing else pins leaves the pair
under-determined. Two contradictory conditions are not diagnosed: the last one written wins.
